behavioral_evidence.value: Popularity-adjusted directed item transitions inside training sequences - for each item i, the multiset N+(i) of items that follow it within a window of 5 positions, with per-pair weight w_ij = cnt(i->j) / sqrt(pop_i * pop_j).

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: Built once, offline, from the training split sequences only (user, item, timestamp ordered): cnt(i->j) counts every ordered pair at distance 1..5 in a user's training sequence; pop_i is the training interaction count; the suffix-popularity normalisation is applied at use time. Stored as a fixed successor table (top 16 by weight per item, 24556 x 16 int32 plus float32 weights). During training the table is read only, and the level-l codes of the successors are taken from the epoch-boundary residual cache, which every rank recomputes identically from the fully replicated content matrix and the replicated codebook.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: The successor table is built from training sequences only; no validation or test sequence is read by the offline script, and the curvature quotient uses the frozen baseline RQ-VAE whose Stage-2 fit used the training split only. The null-standardised curvature is reduced to three scalars delta_1..delta_3 that are shipped as configuration constants, so nothing about validation or test can enter the SID construction at run time, and no validation-selected constant exists: lambda comes from a measured median, R from a measured median, the strength s from the measured delta, the kernel's 1/2 is the Gaussian default, T = 3 is a documented default, and neither lambda nor T is ever varied.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the Stage-2 training split only: count directed item transitions (s_t, s_{t+1}) over all training sequences; map each item to its current level-l Euclidean code; aggregate into the weighted directed quotient graph W^l on the K codes; compute Ollivier-Ricci curvature per edge with lazy random walk (alpha=0.5) and shortest-path ground distance; average over edges to kappa_hat_l; standardise against R=20 nulls obtained by permuting item-to-code membership within the level while preserving each code's item count; delta_l = z_l - mean_l z_l.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: The graph, its curvature, the null and the lambda margin calibration are built only from Stage-2 training sequences and Stage-2 training item embeddings, in a pre-pass that finishes before the training loop. No validation or test sequence, no validation or test co-occurrence and no validation or test code histogram enters delta, lambda, the codebook or the swap rule. Stage-3 items receive their SIDs from the frozen encoder plus the frozen rule; their own interactions are never read. Because delta is a 3-vector saved to config, there is no rank-dependent quantity and no in-loop all-reduce.

behavioral_evidence.claim: the proposed training-only signal
behavioral_evidence.value: Popularity-adjusted directed successor lift over training sequences, turned into a per-item successor set S_i with weights w_ij, and thence into a per-level successor-code centroid m_i^(l). Secondary (diagnostic only, never an admission gate): behaviour-conditioned successor agreement at each level.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the TRAINING split only. For each ordered consecutive pair (u_t, u_{t+1}) in every training sequence accumulate t_ij (raw counts, no dedup, no reweighting by position). Popularity margins n_i = sum_j t_ij, m_j = sum_i t_ij. Lift w_ij = t_ij / sqrt((n_i+1)(m_j+1)). S_i = the smallest prefix of the w_ij-sorted successors whose cumulative weight reaches 50% of sum_j w_ij, capped at 16 (B_i = min(16, b_i), floor 1). Then m_i^(l) = sum_{j in S_i} w_ij c^(l)_{e_l(j)} / sum_{j in S_i} w_ij using the FROZEN BASELINE assignment e_l (this breaks the circularity: the centroid never depends on the permutation being optimised). Items with empty S_i get m_i^(l) = 0.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: The transition counts, the successor sets, the quotient graphs and the curvature null distribution are computed exclusively from training-split sequences; no validation or test interaction, item or session is read at any point. The item embeddings and codebooks are the frozen Stage-2 artefacts trained on the training catalogue. The curvature measurement is run ONCE, offline, before the arm starts, on a single process (not inside the training loop), and written to a JSON artifact that every rank reads at start-up, so there is no rank-0-only broadcast or in-loop export; every rank reconstructs identical kappa_l, s_l and q_k from the artifact plus the frozen codebook. Stage-3 is untouched and only measures.

ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage-2 training split only: count directed item transitions (s_t, s_{t+1}) over all training sequences; map each item to its current level-l Euclidean code; aggregate into the weighted directed quotient graph W^l on the K codes; compute Ollivier-Ricci curvature per edge with lazy random walk (alpha=0.5) and shortest-path ground distance; average over edges to kappa_hat_l; standardise against R=20 nulls obtained by permuting item-to-code membership within the level while preserving each code's item count; delta_l = z_l - mean_l z_l.
ideas.behavior_signal: Standardised, mean-zero behaviour-graph curvature deviation delta_l of the training item-transition quotient graph at each RQ level, measured against a size-preserving member-shuffle null.
ideas.cost_estimate: Offline: quotient graphs have <=256 nodes per level; 3 levels x 21 curvature evaluations (1 real + 20 nulls), Sinkhorn 50 iterations ~ 3.3e6 ops each, plus one pass over 24556 residuals x 256 x 3 for the margins: under 1-2 min on one GPU (or a few minutes CPU), executed before Stage 2, outside the training loop. Per step at the frozen scale (n~1023 items, K=256, L=3): 3 x 262k Poincare distances (~20 flops each) = ~16 MFLOP plus 3 x (262k cost entries + 2 x 262k exchange comparisons) ~ 2.4M scalar ops, i.e. roughly +5 to +15 percent step time over the baseline RQ forward/backward; ~+0.2 to +1 s per epoch, ~+10 to +50 min over the 3000-epoch run. No extra epochs, no extra forward passes.
ideas.coupling_equation: b_ik = lambda_l * delta_l * [ d_P(u_i, v_k) - (1/K) sum_{k'} d_P(u_i, v_{k'}) ], with delta_l the standardised training-split behaviour-graph curvature deviation and d_P the fixed-curvature Poincare distance; the assignment minimises C_ik + b_ik subject to the exact code histogram m_k.
ideas.coupling_path: training transitions -> quotient graph -> standardised curvature profile delta_l -> additive assignment bias b_ik = lambda_l * delta_l * centred d_P(u_i, v_k) -> quota-preserving swap -> digit a_i -> codebook update and Stage-2 sequence of SIDs. delta_l enters only through b, and d_P enters only through b, so setting delta=0 or replacing d_P by a Euclidean distance changes the digits.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If delta_l>0 means the level's behaviour quotient is more clustered than its size-preserving null, then a positive bias on d_P (penalising codes far from the item in the Poincare ball) reinforces the clusters the behaviour graph already shows, while delta_1<0 (fine level under-curved) pushes the fine digit away from hyperbolic proximity, i.e. separates items that the null says are not neighbours. If the coarse digit becomes more behaviourally predictable from its prefix, the frozen Stage 3 beam should find the right level-3 group more often, and test_recall@10 should exceed the baseline 0.055537 and approach 0.065, while the per-level histograms, the 247/7414/20223 supports and the 0.177 collision are unchanged by construction.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Exclusively in the discrete SID assignment step of each RQ level (the choice of which code digit each training item gets), as an additive term in the assignment cost; it never touches the codebook vectors, the EMA update, the encoder gradient or the loss.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare distance in the unit ball of fixed negative curvature -1 (curvature is fixed, never fit and never used to set a radius): d_P(u,v) = arcosh(1 + 2||u-v||^2 / ((1-||u||^2)(1-||v||^2))), applied to tanh-projected residuals and code vectors, with stop-gradient on both arguments.
ideas.key_change: Inside each RQ level, compute the normal Euclidean cost C_ik and the Euclidean assignment a0 with code histogram m_k; then add b_ik = lambda_l * delta_l * d_P(u_i, v_k) (centred over k) to the cost and run a fixed number of count-preserving item-code SWAPS starting from a0. The output digit vector has exactly the histogram m_k of the Euclidean argmin, and its digits differ from a0 for a measured set of items.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The graph, its curvature, the null and the lambda margin calibration are built only from Stage-2 training sequences and Stage-2 training item embeddings, in a pre-pass that finishes before the training loop. No validation or test sequence, no validation or test co-occurrence and no validation or test code histogram enters delta, lambda, the codebook or the swap rule. Stage-3 items receive their SIDs from the frozen encoder plus the frozen rule; their own interactions are never read. Because delta is a 3-vector saved to config, there is no rank-dependent quantity and no in-loop all-reduce.
ideas.motivation: The two measured failures are (i) a multiplicative behaviour weight on a Euclidean distance that moved margins but moved no arg-min, and (ii) a codebook whose radius was spent on curvature, collapsing support to 56 triples. What is missing is an assignment mechanism in which the behaviour-curvature signal is ADDITIVE on the cost (so it provably reorders the top-1), the per-level usage multiset is EXACT by construction (so the resolution cannot collapse), and the curvature is spent only as a signed re-ranking pressure, never as a radius.
ideas.novelty: Earlier arms either (a) made curvature set a level/ball scale (CURVCTRL-SID, BRad-RQ, Poincare-Frechet codebook), (b) multiplied a distance by a behaviour weight (CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN), or (c) used a transport plan whose arg-max need not reproduce its marginals. This proposal uses a swap-exact assignment whose invariant is the Euclidean code histogram, and injects the training-split standardised curvature deviation as a zero-mean additive bias times a fixed-curvature Poincare distance held outside the gradient. Removing the behaviour zeroes the bias and the rule provably returns the Euclidean assignment (verified as Hamming 0); removing the curvature replaces d_P by a Euclidean tangent distance on the same ball. Nothing here rescales a code, a ball or a codebook radius.
ideas.observables: (i) Hamming fraction of items whose level-l digit differs from the Euclidean argmin, per level (must be >0 for the coupling to be live; expected 5-25 percent); (ii) an in-code assertion that the level-l histogram equals m_k exactly at every step; (iii) distinct-code support 247/7414/20223 and triple collision near 0.177 (not 0.998); (iv) first-level/second-level/third-level prefix hit rates near 0.079/0.005 as in the baseline and the teacher-forced next-digit NLL per level; (v) Stage-3 test_recall@10 against 0.055537 with the 0.065 target.
risks: The sign of the curvature deviation may be the wrong direction for recall and, with no tuning allowed, a single run loses; the bias is calibrated to the median top-2 margin so it only touches the ambiguous half of the assignment and the effect may be under one point of recall; tanh projection saturates for large residual norms, making d_P nearly constant and the coupling weak; one sweep of swaps may stop in a poor local optimum; the offline curvature is computed on the epoch-0 codebooks and goes stale as the codebook moves; exact quota preservation can still raise triple collisions if the swaps concentrate items, so the collision rate must be watched.
ideas.safeguards: eps=1e-9 in every norm and denominator; arcosh argument clamped to [1,1e6]; ||u||, ||v|| clamped to 1-1e-6; |delta_l| clipped to 1.0; lambda_l floored at 1e-3 and set to the measured median margin ratio (no sweep); stop_gradient on u and v so no curved gradient can move a code or a radius; the ball radius is a constant 1 and the codebook vectors are the baseline Euclidean vectors, so the curvature cannot shrink the space; per-code buckets are only exchanged, never resized, and the histogram equality is asserted each step; the offline job is a single pre-pass writing a config file (no NCCL, no rank-0 broadcast inside the loop); if the measured Hamming distance is 0 the run logs COUPLING-INERT rather than silently claiming the mechanism.
ideas.spec_equations: Pre-pass: W^l_{jk} = #{(t): code_l(s_t)=j, code_l(s_{t+1})=k}; m_j = 0.5 e_j + 0.5 W_j./sum(W_j); kappa(j,k) = 1 - W1(m_j,m_k)/d_G(j,k); kappa_hat_l = mean_{jk: W_jk>0} kappa(j,k); over R=20 membership shuffles pi_r: z_l = (kappa_hat_l - mean_r kappa_hat_l^{(r)})/sd_r; delta_l = z_l - mean_{l'} z_{l'}. Per step, per level: u_i = tanh(||r_i||/2) r_i/(||r_i||+eps); v_k = tanh(||c_k||/2) c_k/(||c_k||+eps); d_ik = arcosh(clamp(1 + 2||u_i-v_k||^2/((1-||u_i||^2)(1-||v_k||^2)+eps), 1, 1e6)); b_ik = lam_l * delta_l * (d_ik - mean_k d_ik); a0 = argmin_k ||r_i-c_k||^2; m = hist(a0); for i in order: j=a_i; for k != j with bucket_k non-empty: i* = argmax_{i' in bucket_k}(||r_{i'}-c_k||^2 + b_{i'k}); if (||r_i-c_k||^2+b_ik) + (||r_{i*}-c_j||^2+b_{i*j}) < (||r_i-c_j||^2+b_ij) + (||r_{i*}-c_k||^2+b_{i*k}) then swap(a_i, a_{i*}). Return a, m.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: per-level training residual batch {r_i}, frozen codebook {c_k}, frozen scalars delta_l and lambda_l, the seed-fixed item order. Outputs: one integer digit a_i per item per level, a per-level digit vector whose histogram is exactly m_k, and the residuals for the next level. The offline input is the training transition list plus the initial codes; the offline output is the 3-vector delta and the 3-vector lambda.

specification.text: (1) Pre-pass on the TRAINING split only: build the weighted quotient transition graph W^l_{jk} by counting training item transitions s_t -> s_{t+1} between the level-l codes j,k of the initial Euclidean codebooks; compute Ollivier-Ricci curvature kappa_e per edge with lazy random walk m_j = 0.5*delta_j + 0.5*W_j./deg_j and d = graph shortest path, kappa_e = 1 - W1(m_j,m_k)/d(j,k); take kappa_hat_l = mean_e kappa_e. (2) Null: R=20 size-preserving member shuffles (permute item->code membership inside each level keeping each code's item count), recompute kappa_hat_l each time; z_l = (kappa_hat_l - mean_null)/sd_null; delta_l = z_l - mean_{l'=1..3} z_{l'}; clip |delta_l| to 1.0. On the frozen baseline this reproduces delta = [-0.328, -0.071, +0.399]. (3) Save delta and a per-level lambda_l to the run config; every rank loads the same file. (4) Per training step (batch of n~1023 items), per level l=1..3 with residual r_i and code c_k: u_i = tanh(||r_i||/2) r_i/||r_i||; v_k = tanh(||c_k||/2) c_k/||c_k|| (both stop-gradient); d_P(u,v) = arcosh(1 + 2||u-v||^2 / ((1-||u||^2)(1-||v||^2) + 1e-9)); C_ik = ||r_i - c_k||^2; a0_i = argmin_k C_ik; m_k = count(a0 = k); lambda_l = median_i(C_{i,a1}-C_{i,a2}) / median_{i,k} d_P (measured once at epoch 0, frozen); b_ik = lambda_l * delta_l * (d_P(u_i,v_k) - mean_k d_P(u_i,v_k)). (5) T=1 sweep (documented default) in a seed-fixed item order: for item i at code j, for each non-empty bucket k != j, let i* = argmax_{i' in bucket k} (C_{i',k}+b_{i',k}); swap i and i* iff (C_ik+b_ik)+(C_{i*,j}+b_{i*,j}) < (C_ij+b_ij)+(C_{i*,k}+b_{i*,k}); update the two buckets. The bucket sizes are never changed, so the histogram is the invariant. (6) Commit digits, form residuals r_i <- r_i - c_{a_i}, keep the baseline reconstruction + commitment loss and the baseline EMA codebook update unchanged. (7) At SID construction time for any split (including Stage 3 items) the same frozen delta, lambda, codebooks and swap rule are applied; test items bring embeddings only, no behaviour.

ideas.title: Quota-preserving SID exchange under an additive, standardised-curvature Poincare proximity bias

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: N+(i) := empty for every item, so v == 0, every swap gain is exactly 0, no transposition is accepted, and the labelling equals the Euclidean pass bit for bit; frac_top1_changed = 0 at every level and Stage 2 reduces to the baseline RQ-VAE.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run above: curved kernel at nu_l = exp(delta_l), behaviour vote from N+(i), additive bias, quota-exact transposition. This is the only arm that is trained.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: The curved operation is replaced by the Euclidean one - delta_l := 0, d_P replaced by ||e_c - e_c'||/R in the kernel, and the Euclidean mean used wherever a curved centroid would be used - while the behaviour vote, the quotas, lambda_l and the swap search are unchanged.
ideas.behavior_computation: Built once, offline, from the training split sequences only (user, item, timestamp ordered): cnt(i->j) counts every ordered pair at distance 1..5 in a user's training sequence; pop_i is the training interaction count; the suffix-popularity normalisation is applied at use time. Stored as a fixed successor table (top 16 by weight per item, 24556 x 16 int32 plus float32 weights). During training the table is read only, and the level-l codes of the successors are taken from the epoch-boundary residual cache, which every rank recomputes identically from the fully replicated content matrix and the replicated codebook.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted directed item transitions inside training sequences - for each item i, the multiset N+(i) of items that follow it within a window of 5 positions, with per-pair weight w_ij = cnt(i->j) / sqrt(pop_i * pop_j).
ideas.cost_estimate: Only level 3 executes (s = [0,0,1] on the evidence). Added per step at 1023 x 256 x 32: cost matrix 8.4 MFLOP, codebook kernel 256x256x32 = 2.1 MFLOP, sparse vote 1023x16x256 = 4.2 MFLOP, three swap passes ~1.6 MFLOP, total ~16 MFLOP per step against the baseline's level-3 assignment of ~8.4 MFLOP, i.e. 2-3x the RQ-VAE assignment work and roughly 1.4-2x Stage-2 wall clock over 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72,000 steps (tens of minutes, four cards). Epoch-boundary residual cache refresh over all 24556 items is 0.4 GFLOP per epoch, 1.2 TFLOP total, minutes. Offline curvature precompute: transition graph a few million edges, Ollivier W1 per edge under 32 member-shuffle draws, a few minutes to ~20 minutes once on CPU. Memory +0.3 MB (batch x C plus C x C). Stage 3 is untouched and runs the frozen protocol.
ideas.coupling_equation: S_l(i,c) = || r_{l-1}(i) - e_c ||^2  +  lambda_l * ( - [ sum_{j in N+(i)} w_ij * exp( - d_P^{exp(delta_l)}( e_c/R , e_{c_l(j)}/R )^2 / 2 ) ] / [ sum_{j in N+(i)} w_ij ] ), with lambda_l = s_l * median_i ||r_{l-1}(i) - e_{cE(i)}||^2 and s_l = [delta_l]_+ / sum_{l'} [delta_l']_+.
ideas.coupling_path: training transitions -> per-item successor vote over codewords -> vote spread by the Poincare kernel at curvature exp(delta_l) -> additive term lambda_l * (-v(i,c)) in the assignment cost -> quota-preserving transposition -> final level-l label -> codebook sum update and SID token. Removing the behaviour empties N+(i) so the vote is identically zero and the cost collapses to the Euclidean one, which leaves no accepted transposition; removing the curved operation replaces d_P by the Euclidean distance in the kernel, which changes the spread of every vote and therefore the argmin set. Neither half is a side term: both are operands of the same kernel-weighted vote.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Worth keeping iff (i) the vote materially reorders the fine level - frac_top1_changed_3 between roughly 0.08 and 0.30 with levels 1 and 2 at exactly 0 - and (ii) that reordering raises the fine-token conditional predictability of the true next item without raising collisions. Observed as: distinct-triple count stays near 7414 (it cannot fall below the baseline level-1 pattern because that level is bit-identical), first-level hit rates stay at 0.079/0.005, collision near 0.177, and Stage3 test_recall@10 > 0.055537 with 0.065 as the target. If frac_top1_changed_3 is under 0.02 the coupling is present but inert and the idea is dead regardless of recall.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In the assignment cost only, at the level(s) with delta_l > 0, inside the codebook-to-codebook kernel that spreads the training-successor vote. It does not touch the codebook vectors, the codebook radius, the quotas, or the residual computation.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball exponential and distance at trainable-free, measurement-derived negative curvature nu_l = exp(delta_l) (dimensionless in units of R): exp_0^nu(v) = tanh(sqrt(nu)||v||/2) v/||v||, and d_P^nu(x,y) = (1/sqrt(nu)) arcosh(1 + 2 nu ||x-y||^2 / ((1 - nu||x||^2)(1 - nu||y||^2))), with the ball radius 1/sqrt(nu).
ideas.key_change: At each RQ level the Euclidean residual argmin is computed first and its per-codeword counts are frozen as quotas; every training successor of item i then casts a weight w_ij at the level-l codeword it currently occupies, that vote is spread over codewords by a Poincare kernel exp(-d_P(v_l)^2/2) evaluated at curvature exp(delta_l) on R-normalised codebook coordinates, and the negated vote enters the assignment cost as an ADDITIVE term whose magnitude is the level's own measured median reconstruction distortion. The item-to-codeword labelling is then improved by accepted transpositions only, so the Euclidean usage multiset is reproduced exactly.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The successor table is built from training sequences only; no validation or test sequence is read by the offline script, and the curvature quotient uses the frozen baseline RQ-VAE whose Stage-2 fit used the training split only. The null-standardised curvature is reduced to three scalars delta_1..delta_3 that are shipped as configuration constants, so nothing about validation or test can enter the SID construction at run time, and no validation-selected constant exists: lambda comes from a measured median, R from a measured median, the strength s from the measured delta, the kernel's 1/2 is the Gaussian default, T = 3 is a documented default, and neither lambda nor T is ever varied.
ideas.motivation: The baseline TIGER_RQ-VAE (247/7414/20223, Stage3 test_recall@10 = 0.055537) clusters items purely by content, so a fine (level-3) token says "this item looks like these items" and not "this item sits on this behavioural branch". The generative model therefore has to guess branch identity from content evidence alone. Round 1 tried to fix this by spending the measured behaviour-graph curvature on the SID space radius and the codebook collapsed (170 -> 56 distinct triples, recall 0.041888); round 2 tried to fix it with a multiplicative per-pair cost weight and the verifier measured 0 of 4 argmins moving. The problem is real (the level-3 behaviour quotient is more tree-like than its size-preserving null, delta_3 = +0.399) but it needs a mechanism whose top-1 effect is provable and whose capacity effect is zero.
ideas.novelty: Three things that no earlier arm here did. (i) The behaviour term is a bounded PROBABILITY-like vote, not a distance rescale: v(i,c) in [0,1], so its top-1 effect is an absolute cost gap rather than a ratio gap and cannot be a no-op on non-equidistant codes. (ii) The assignment object is not a soft plan and not a radius: quotas are read off the Euclidean pass and then the labelling is changed only by composing transpositions of two items' labels, so the per-level usage multiset is invariant BY CONSTRUCTION with nothing to assert about marginals. (iii) The curvature is spent INSIDE the kernel metric used to spread the vote (curvature nu_l = exp(delta_l) on R-normalised coordinates), so it changes which codeword a behaviour vote lands on while leaving codebook vectors, radii and counts untouched; and the sign-gated strength s_l = [delta_l]_+ / sum [delta_l]_+ spends it only where the measured quotient is genuinely above its null, which on the evidence is level 3 alone.
ideas.observables: Per level, frac_top1_changed_l = |{i : a_l(i) != cE_l(i)}| / n; expected [0, 0, 0.08-0.30]. The count of distinct used level-1 codes must stay exactly 247 (it is invariant by construction); distinct triples stay near 7414 rather than collapsing toward the 56-170 range of round 1; collision stays near 0.177; first-level hit rates stay at 0.079/0.005 because level 1 is bit-identical; the level-l codebook sum norms move away from the baseline even though the counts do not; and Stage3 test_recall@10 is read once against 0.055537.
risks: (1) Co-consumed items are content-similar, so the vote may mostly agree with the Euclidean argmin and few swaps survive the cost test - the mechanism becomes a no-op and recall is unchanged. (2) Because the cost test includes the Euclidean distortion, the swaps may concentrate on poorly reconstructed, low-margin items and change nothing that matters. (3) The level-3-only gate makes the effect small: one token of three changes for a minor fraction of items, so even a correct mechanism may only move recall by a few thousandths. (4) The hyperbolic kernel may be numerically close to the Euclidean kernel for codewords at similar radii, making the geometry-off arm nearly identical to both-on; this is the specific comparison that must be reported, not assumed. (5) Successor votes taken from the previous epoch's cache lag by up to 24 steps and could reinforce an early accident.
ideas.safeguards: arcosh argument clamped to >= 1 + 1e-7 and the denominator to >= 1e-9; ball coordinates clipped at ||z|| <= 0.997/sqrt(nu_l), which is safe because R is chosen so the median point sits at tanh(exp(delta_l/2)/2) ~ 0.46 of the ball radius; kernel exponent floored at -60; v floored at 0 and capped at 1 (it is a convex combination, so this is only float hygiene); lambda_l floored at 1e-6 * mean_i ||x_i||^2 so a degenerate level cannot produce a zero-cost bias; if the batch has fewer than two distinct occupied codewords, or if max_c v(i,c) - min_c v(i,c) < 1e-8 for every i, the swap search exits early and the labelling equals the Euclidean pass; all reductions are over full replicated tensors so every rank computes the identical delta, R, s and cache and no broadcast, collective or rank-0 read happens inside the training loop; no random tie-breaking anywhere (ties broken by lowest codeword index) so the run is exactly reproducible.
ideas.spec_equations:
Offline:
  cnt(i->j) from training sequences, window 5; w_ij = cnt(i->j)/sqrt(pop_i pop_j); keep top 16.
  R = median_i ||x_i||.
  for l in 1..3: build quotient graph over baseline level-l prefix groups, W_l(alpha,beta) = sum_{i in alpha, j in beta} cnt(i->j); kappa(alpha,beta) = 1 - W1(m_alpha, m_beta)/d(alpha,beta) with lazy (1/2) walk measures;
    null: 32 draws of a size-preserving member shuffle (permute item->group membership, preserve group sizes and the edge total); kappa_hat(alpha,beta) = (kappa - mu_null)/sigma_null;
    kappa_hat_l = edge-weight-weighted mean; delta_l = kappa_hat_l - mean_l kappa_hat_l.
  s_l = [delta_l]_+ / sum_l' [delta_l']_+  (if all zero: s = one-hot at argmax delta_l).
Per step:
  for l in 1..3:
    if s_l == 0: a_l = cE_l; continue        # baseline path, unchanged
    z = tanh(sqrt(nu_l)||e/R||/2) * (e/R)/||e/R||            # [C,d]
    D = arcosh(1 + 2 nu_l ||z_c - z_c'||^2 / ((1-nu_l||z_c||^2)(1-nu_l||z_c'||^2))) / sqrt(nu_l)
    Khat = exp(-D*D/2)                                       # [C,C]
    v[i,c] = sum_j w_ij*Khat[c, cache(j)] / sum_j w_ij        # [B,C], 0 if N+(i) empty
    lambda = median_i ||r_{l-1}(i) - e_{cE(i)}||^2
    S = ||r_{l-1}(i) - e_c||^2 - lambda * v
    a = cE
    for t in 1..3:
      cs = argmin_c S; g = S[i,a[i]] - S[i,cs]                 # g >= 0
      bucket[p,q] = argmax_{i: a[i]=p, cs[i]=q, g[i]>0} g[i]    # scatter-max over p*C+q
      for each unordered pair {p,q} with both buckets filled:
        i = bucket[p,q]; j = bucket[q,p]
        if S[i,q] + S[j,p] < S[i,p] + S[j,q]: swap labels of i and j
    return a, with counts(a) == counts(cE) by the transposition lemma
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: level-l residuals r_{l-1}(batch) [B,d], codebook E_l [C,d], successor table N+ with weights [B,16], successor level-l Euclidean codes from the epoch cache [B,16], the offline constants delta_l and R, and s_l. Outputs: the final level-l label a_l(i) for every item in the batch (feeding the codebook EMA/update and the SID token), plus the diagnostics frac_top1_changed_l and the count multiset q(c). Side output for the next epoch: refreshed full-set residuals and Euclidean codes.

specification.text:
Notation: level l in {1,2,3}; codebook E_l = {e_c}, c = 1..256; r_{l-1}(i) is the level-l input residual; R = median_i ||x_i|| over the 24556 training content embeddings (offline, one scalar).
Offline constants (a 3-vector shipped in the config): delta_l = kappa_hat_l - mean_l(kappa_hat_l), where kappa_hat_l is the edge-weight-weighted mean of the null-standardised Ollivier curvatures of the training behaviour quotient at the frozen baseline SIDs' level-l prefixes. On the measured evidence delta = [-0.328, -0.071, +0.399].
Per step, per level l (levels with s_l = 0 are skipped entirely and are bit-identical to the baseline):
1. Euclidean pass: cE(i) = argmin_c ||r_{l-1}(i) - e_c||^2; quotas q(c) = |{i in batch : cE(i) = c}|.
2. Ball map: nu_l = exp(delta_l); z_c = exp_0^{nu_l}(e_c / R), with exp_0^nu(v) = tanh(sqrt(nu)||v||/2) v/||v||.
3. Kernel: Khat[c,c'] = exp( -d_P^{nu_l}(z_c, z_c')^2 / 2 ), distances in R units.
4. Successor vote: v(i,c) = sum_{j in N+(i)} w_ij Khat[c, c_l^cache(j)] / sum_{j in N+(i)} w_ij, and v(i,c) = 0 if N+(i) is empty; c_l^cache is the previous-epoch-end level-l Euclidean code of j.
5. Additive cost: S(i,c) = ||r_{l-1}(i) - e_c||^2 - lambda_l * v(i,c), with lambda_l = s_l * median_i ||r_{l-1}(i) - e_{cE(i)}||^2.
6. Quota-exact permutation by swap local search (T = 3 passes, no cap on accepted swaps): described in SPEC EQUATIONS.
7. The final labelling drives the usual codebook EMA/update; the geometry and the kernel are detached (no gradient through the hyperbolic map).

ideas.title: Exact-quota hyperbolic vote assignment: an additive curvature-kernel behaviour bias that permutes RQ slots without ever touching the usage multiset

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: eta_l <- 0 for all l, so Bias is identically zero and C reduces to the normalised curved distance. The switch exists as one config flag read at every level and is correct in the code; it is exercised only in no-grad inference passes over the finished model and never as a trained arm, so no second training run is spent.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The trained arm: Poincare distance, tangent-space codebook EMA, and eta_l * kappa_hat_l(a0_i,k) * successor mass, minimised by the quota-exact 12-round 2-swap descent. One run, 3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping, no sweep, no multi-seed.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: d_P replaced by the Euclidean norm and the tangent-space codebook EMA replaced by a plain mean, with phi kept as a fixed squashing map so everything else in the code path is identical. Also exercised only in inference passes on the single trained model.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the TRAIN split only. For every consecutive pair (i -> j) inside a training sequence, w_ij += 1. Then w_i(k) = sum over j with pi_l(j)=k of w_ij and w_i = sum over j of w_ij, with pi_l the level-l prefix map of the frozen baseline. Stored offline as a CSR over the 24556 training items for the three levels, then frozen.
ideas.behavior_signal: Training-only directed item transitions, aggregated into a per-item successor distribution over level-l codes and entered as the successor mass w_i(k)/w_i at each of the three levels.
ideas.cost_estimate: Per step at the frozen scale (24556 training items, 24 steps per epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps): 3 levels x 1024 x 256 = 786k Poincare distance evaluations, about 16 MFLOP, plus 3 x 12 rounds x (B*K + K*K) roughly 12 MFLOP, plus three host synchronisations to read the fixed-round result, so about 3-6 ms per step on an A100-class card, roughly 5-10% over the baseline step, about 6 minutes of added wall clock over the whole run. Memory: artifact 20-30 MB, memory-mapped, no per-rank copy. Offline build: one CPU pass over training sequences plus 32 shuffles x 3 levels x 2000 sampled edges, 25-45 minutes once, outside the four-card Stage 2 budget.
ideas.coupling_equation: C[i,k] = d_P(x_i, e_k) / m_l  +  eta_l * clip(kappa_hat_l(a0_i, k), -4, +4) * (w_i(k) / w_i)
ideas.coupling_path: successor mass w_i(k)/w_i (behaviour) times standardised behaviour-graph curvature kappa_hat_l(a0_i,k) times the level deviation eta_l gives an additive term; that term enters C[i,k]; C drives the quota-preserving swaps; the swaps decide the item's code triple, which is the token sequence Stage 3 trains on. Setting eta_l = 0 removes the term and the descent from a0 makes only the moves the curved metric alone justifies, so the emitted SIDs change; replacing d_P by the Euclidean distance changes a0, the protected multiset, the normalised distances and therefore every swap decision. Neither can be dropped without changing the SIDs.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: That the standardised behaviour-graph curvature of a level identifies which successor codes a code should be allowed to reach, so reallocating items between codes under that additive bias places co-transitioning items in shared prefixes more often without moving a single usage count. If true: the per-level swap rate is non-zero at levels 1 and 3 and near zero at level 2; prefix-bigram top-1 accuracy of level 2 given level 1 and of level 3 given levels 1-2 rises against the same model with the bias off; distinct prefix counts stay near 247/7414/20223 and the collision rate stays near 0.177 because the multiset is invariant; and Stage 3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 against the 0.055537 baseline. If the swap rate is below about 1% at every level, the hypothesis is already false at the assignment and the recall result is interpretable without further experiments.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In the RQ-VAE quantizer at Stage 2: the assignment cost of all three levels, the straight-through commitment loss, and the EMA codebook update (tangent-space barycentre at the origin). It does not act inside Stage 3.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball distance d_P(x,y) = 2 artanh(||(-x) xor y||) with fixed curvature c = 1, together with the exponential and logarithmic maps exp_0/log_0 used for the codebook update and the parameter-free ball map phi(z) = z/(1+||z||).
ideas.key_change: (1) Encoder outputs and code vectors are mapped into the unit Poincare ball, the quantization distance becomes d_P at fixed curvature c=1, and the codebook EMA is carried in the tangent space at the origin. (2) Inside each level and each rank-local batch shard, the code of item i is chosen by a cost that adds a curvature-weighted successor-mass bias to the normalised curved distance, and that cost is minimised by exact 2-swaps starting from the Euclidean nearest assignment, so the multiset can never move.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Both inputs to the artifact are train-only: transition counts come from training sequences, and pi_l comes from the frozen baseline evaluated on the 24556 training items. Validation and test sequences are never referenced by the artifact script, the artifact is frozen before Stage 2 starts, and no per-epoch statistic enters it, so no validation or test interaction can reach the SID construction.
ideas.motivation: The baseline TIGER RQ-VAE gives every training item the code triple nearest to it in an isotropic Euclidean residual space, so a SID carries no information about where the item sits in the training transition graph, and two items users actually consume in sequence frequently get different prefixes. Round 1 spent the measured behaviour-graph curvature on the space's radius and destroyed the codebook (170 -> 56 distinct triples, Stage3 recall 0.041888). Round 2 put behaviour in as a multiplicative per-pair weight: margins moved, not one argmin did. What is missing is a behaviour term that provably changes which code an item receives, plus a resolution guarantee that survives any curved metric, however aggressive.
ideas.novelty: The assignment is constrained to be a PERMUTATION of the Euclidean nearest-neighbour assignment of the same batch shard: a sequence of transpositions. The per-level usage multiset is therefore invariant by construction (every code keeps exactly the count the baseline quantizer gave it, so collision rate and exposure are unchanged), while WHICH item holds which code is re-decided by an additive curved-plus-curvature cost. No Sinkhorn plan, no marginal argmax, no rescaling of distances, no radius, temperature or usage-weight parameter, no codebook renormalisation. The behaviour-graph curvature is spent as an additive per-pair cost term and never as a scale.
ideas.observables: (i) per-level swap rate s_l = |{i : a[i] != a0[i]}| / B at epochs 1, 500, 1500, 3000, which is exactly 0 when the bias is off and the metric perturbation is absent; (ii) the usage-multiset difference sorted(a)-sorted(a0), which must be exactly 0 at every logged step; (iii) distinct prefix counts per level against 247/7414/20223, and the collision rate against 0.177; (iv) prefix-bigram top-1 predictability on held-out training tails; (v) the fraction of items with no training successor; (vi) the number of binding swap rounds out of 12; (vii) Stage 3 test_recall@10 against 0.055537.
risks: eta_2 is small (-0.24), so the middle level may barely move and a third of the mechanism may be inert; the quotient is built on the frozen baseline's prefixes and is therefore a static prior that can drift from the codebook being trained; the 12-round budget may bind and leave the descent far from its local optimum; the Poincare metric concentrates distances near the boundary and, although the quota forbids collapse, it may still push unrelated items into rare codes and hurt prefix predictability; the bias magnitude (eta * kappa_hat * successor mass, typically 0.1-0.4 against a normalised distance spread near 1) may be too small to move enough items, in which case the measured swap rate is exactly the diagnostic that says so.
ideas.safeguards: artanh via 0.5*log((1+r)/(1-r)) with r pre-clamped to 1-1e-6; ||x|| and ||e|| clamped to 1-1e-3 before every Poincare operation; Mobius denominator clamped at 1e-9; kappa_hat hard-clipped at four null standard deviations; items with no outgoing training transition get Bias = 0 and keep a0, and their coverage fraction is logged; m_l is the median of the previous epoch's per-batch median curved distance, a measured quantity refreshed once per epoch and never selected; sum_k q[k] == B and sorted(a) == sorted(a0) are asserted device-side every step on every rank, a violation raises; no torch.distributed call exists in the offline script or in the assignment path, and the artifact is read through a memory map so each rank touches only its own rows; the descent is run with a fixed round count so no data-dependent host branch is taken inside the loop.
ideas.spec_equations: d_P(x,y) = 2 artanh(||(-x) xor y||), c = 1; phi(z) = z/(1+||z||); e_k = phi(theta_k); a0 = argmin_k ||x_i - e_k||; q[k] = |{i : a0[i]=k}|; Bias[i,k] = eta_l * clip(kappa_hat_l(a0[i],k),-4,4) * w_i(k)/w_i; C[i,k] = d_P(x_i,e_k)/m_l + Bias[i,k]; M[i,k] = C[i,k] - C[i,a[i]]; A[p,r] = min_{i:a[i]=p} M[i,r]; G[p,r] = A[p,r] + A[r,p]; a <- swap(argmin_{p,r} G) while min G < 0, at most 12 rounds; invariant sorted(a) == sorted(a0); kappa_hat_l(a,b) = clip((kappa_l(a,b)-mu_l)/sigma_l,-4,4); eta_l = delta_l/std(delta); t_k <- (1-gamma) t_k + gamma * mean_{i in k} log_0(x_i), gamma = 0.99; e_k = exp_0(t_k).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are the batch encoder outputs h (B x d), the current three codebooks, and the frozen train-only artifact (kappa_hat key-value arrays per level, CSR successor masses, eta_l, m_l seeds). Output is, for every item, a triple of code indices, i.e. its SID, plus per-level swap counts and the multiset assertion result. The Stage 3 recommender consumes the triples unchanged; only Stage 2 changes.

specification.text:
Offline, once, on CPU before Stage 2 (no collectives, one artifact memory-mapped by all ranks):
  1. w_ij = directed transition counts over TRAIN-split sequences only, i,j in the 24556 training items.
  2. pi_l(i) = level-l prefix of training item i under the FROZEN baseline RQ-VAE (train items only).
  3. Quotient graph per level: W_l(a,b) = sum over i with pi_l(i)=a and j with pi_l(j)=b of w_ij.
  4. Per edge (a,b) with W_l>0, Ollivier curvature with the alpha=0.5 lazy random walk:
     kappa_l(a,b) = 1 - W1(a,b)/d(a,b), W1 = sum_{u,v} mu_a(u) mu_b(v) d(u,v),
     mu_a(u) = alpha*1[u=a] + (1-alpha)*W_l(a,u)/deg_l(a), d = unweighted shortest path on the quotient.
  5. Null: S=32 size-preserving member shuffles; each shuffle reassigns items to prefixes drawn without replacement from the list in which each prefix appears n_a times, so the prefix-size multiset is preserved; kappa is recomputed on a FIXED sample of 2000 edges per level per shuffle and all values are pooled into mu_l, sigma_l.
  6. kappa_hat_l(a,b) = clip((kappa_l(a,b) - mu_l)/sigma_l, -4, +4); kappa_bar_l = mean over quotient edges;
     delta_l = kappa_bar_l - mean_l'(kappa_bar_l'); eta_l = delta_l / std_l'(delta_l').
  7. Artifact acceptance check: |kappa_bar_l - [-2.32,-1.80,-0.86]_l| <= 0.15 for all three levels, otherwise abort.
  Training loop, per step, per level l=1..3, per rank's local shard (no cross-rank call anywhere):
      x_i = phi(h_i), e_k = phi(theta_k), phi(z) = z/(1+||z||) so ||x||<1
      D[i,k] = d_P(x_i, e_k)
      a0[i] = argmin_k ||x_i - e_k||          # Euclidean nearest: quota reference (baseline quantizer's own choice)
      q[k] = |{i : a0[i] = k}|                # the protected multiset, exactly
      Bias[i,k] = eta_l * kappa_hat_l(a0[i], k) * w_i(k)/w_i, on item i's successor-code support, zero elsewhere
      C[i,k] = D[i,k]/m_l + Bias[i,k]
      a <- a0; for round = 1..12 (documented default):
          M[i,k] = C[i,k] - C[i,a[i]]                       # regret of moving i to k
          A[p,r] = min over {i : a[i]=p} of M[i,r]          # scatter-amin, O(B*K)
          G[p,r] = A[p,r] + A[r,p]                          # best 2-swap gain between codes p and r
          (p*,r*) = argmin G; if G[p*,r*] < 0, swap the two argmin items, else leave
      commit a[i]; residual r_i <- r_i - e_{a[i]}; proceed to level l+1
  Loss: curved commitment d_P(x,e)^2 with stop-gradient on the code, plus the reconstruction term unchanged.
  Codebook: t_k <- (1-gamma) t_k + gamma * mean_{i assigned to k} log_0(x_i); e_k = exp_0(t_k), gamma = 0.99 baseline default.

ideas.title: Curvature-biased, quota-exact 2-swap code assignment for a Poincare-ball RQ-VAE

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: p_i = delta_i, hence m_i = x_i, g_i = x_i, the bracket is identically zero, cost reduces to the pure curved nearest-code cost, and B is the quota-exact curved assignment with no successor information.
ideas.ablation_both_on: kappa = 1, geodesic fraction t_l = sigmoid(delta_l), successor Frechet means and the additive bias active, quotas exact; this is the single trained run.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: kappa -> 0: d_P -> Euclidean norm, exp/log -> linear interpolation, m_i -> weighted Euclidean mean; the same additive bias, quotas and deferred acceptance are kept, so only the curvature is removed.
ideas.behavior_computation: Sparse count matrix T[i,j] over training sessions; row-normalised to p_i; used only through the weighted Frechet mean m_i and hence the bias d_P(g_i,E_c) - d_P(x_i,E_c). Items with no successor get p_i = delta_i and zero bias. Recomputed once offline from the training split, never from validation or test.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transitions from training sequences (next-item co-occurrence within a session, unit window), aggregated over the training split only.
ideas.cost_estimate: Per training step the extra work is the hyperbolic map plus one extra distance row on 1024 items x 256 codes x 3 levels = 786k pairs, about +10-20% of the quantiser block (well under +5% of the total transformer step). Each refresh costs 3 x 24556 x 256 = 18.9M cost entries, 24556 x deg Frechet steps, and a deferred-acceptance solve of typically 3-6 rounds of 24556-item proposal sorts: about 0.2 s on one card, under a minute for 30 refreshes, under 1% of the 3000-epoch, 24-step-per-epoch run. No extra parameters, no extra seeds, no arm.
ideas.coupling_equation: cost(i,c) = d_P(x_i,E_c)^2 + lambda_l * [ d_P( exp_{x_i}( sigmoid(delta_l) * log_{x_i}( m_i ) ), E_c ) - d_P(x_i,E_c) ], with m_i = argmin_x sum_j p_i(j) d_P(x,E_j)^2.
ideas.coupling_path: p_i -> m_i (Frechet mean under d_P) -> g_i (geodesic pull by t_l = sigmoid(delta_l)) -> additive bias -> cost matrix -> deferred acceptance -> hard SID B -> STE gradient and next-item prefix statistics. Removing behaviour sets the bias to zero; removing geometry replaces d_P and the Frechet mean by their Euclidean counterparts and changes g_i, so both change the arg-min and the gradient.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If successor-coherent items are placed into the same coarse prefixes under an exactly preserved usage histogram, then the level-1 hit rate stays at its baseline support (0.079/0.005) and the triple collision near 0.177, while prefix next-item predictability rises and Stage3 test_recall@10 moves above the 0.055537 baseline toward 0.065. Observable: the behaviour-off assignment differs from the both-on assignment on 20-60% of items at the last refresh (non-zero top-1 change is REQUIRED and is logged at every refresh), the usage-multiset assertion holds with equality at every refresh, and prefix transition entropy falls at fixed usage.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the quantisation/assignment step of Stage-2 training, on every assignment refresh; it never touches the codebook parameters, the encoder parameterisation, or the latent radius.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball distance d_P with fixed negative curvature kappa = 1 (unit ball), plus the exponential map exp_x and logarithm map log_x used for the geodesic interpolation exp_{x_i}(t_l log_{x_i}(m_i)); the standardised training-graph curvature delta_l sets t_l = sigmoid(delta_l), not the curvature itself.
ideas.key_change: For every training item and every level, a hyperbolic Frechet mean of its training successors is pulled a curvature-determined fraction along the geodesic from the item, and the resulting point contributes an ADDITIVE bias to the item-code cost; the hard SID is then chosen by a capacity-exact deferred-acceptance pass whose per-code capacities are the Euclidean nearest-code counts, so the usage multiset is reproduced exactly while the membership, and therefore the gradient, is behaviour- and curvature-dependent.
ideas.leakage_boundary: T is built from the training interaction sequences only; the curvature profile is computed on the training-item prefix partition only; delta and t are frozen scalars in the config before Stage 2 starts; no validation/test interaction, no Stage-3 label enters the bias, the quotas or the assignment; the quota pass reads only training items.
ideas.motivation: The round-1 arm spent curvature on the radius of the latent ball and the codebook collapsed from 170 to 56 distinct triples (recall 0.0419, below its own parent). The round-2 arm multiplied the transport cost by a per-pair behaviour weight; margins moved but not one arg-min did, so the behaviour dependency was uncertifiable, and its frozen plan did not reproduce its column marginals. The real problem is therefore not "more curvature" but: get behaviour into the arg-min as an ADDITIVE, order-changing term, and protect the per-level usage multiset EXACTLY rather than approximately. Recommendation-wise, what is missing in TIGER SIDs is that two items a user actually jumps between often land in different coarse prefixes, which destroys prefix-level next-item predictability.
ideas.novelty: (i) The codebook is never moved and never re-parameterised: the curved operation acts only on the discrete assignment, so curvature cannot act as a radius/scale on the codebook. (ii) The curvature is spent as a DIRECTION and DISTANCE ALONG A GEODESIC set by the measured, null-standardised behaviour-graph curvature, not as a metric scale: kappa is fixed at 1 and delta_l only sets the geodesic fraction t_l. (iii) The assignment is a capacity-constrained deferred-acceptance (many-to-one Gale-Shapley) allocation whose output has the Euclidean per-level usage multiset EXACTLY by counting, not by a plan's arg-max - this is the direct answer to failure (b). (iv) Unlike the round-1 successor-Frechet codebook update, the successor Frechet mean here is a per-item additive bias on a quota-exact integer assignment, and unlike the round-2 cost reweighting it changes the arg-min by construction because it is added, not multiplied.
ideas.observables: (1) top-1 flip count of B between the behaviour-on and behaviour-off cost at the final refresh (must be > 0 and is logged per refresh); (2) exact equality of the per-level usage multiset of B with the Euclidean m_c^l (asserted); (3) per-level distinct-code counts 247/7414/20223-scale support and collision near 0.177; (4) level-1 hit rates near 0.079/0.005; (5) prefix transition entropy and next-prefix predictability; (6) Stage3 test_recall@10.
risks: The bias may over-pull items toward popular successor codes and destroy within-prefix diversity; deferred acceptance may produce worse-cost matchings than the Euclidean arg-min (it is stable, not optimal), so the reconstruction could degrade; event-triggered refreshes may lag the encoder; the standardised curvature delta may be too weak to set a useful t_l; the Euclidean quota may be a bad capacity target if the baseline usage is very skewed.
ideas.safeguards: clamp ||x|| and ||E|| to 1-1e-3 before artanh; artanh argument clamped to 1-1e-6; log_x(m) at m = x returns 0 (add 1e-8 norm guard); items with empty successor sets get zero bias; lambda_l guarded against a zero median denominator; the deferred-acceptance solve has a hard round cap of 4*K and falls back to the previous B (never to an unconstrained arg-min) if it does not terminate; exact-marginal assertion is a hard gate per refresh; no code may receive more than m_c items because capacity is decremented at accept time.
ideas.spec_equations:
p_i(j) = T[i,j] / sum_k T[i,k]
  m_i^(0) = x_i; m_i^(s+1) = exp_m( eta * sum_j p_i(j) * log_m(x_j) ), eta = 1/sum_j p_i(j), s = 0..4, reproject to ||m|| <= 1-1e-3
  g_i = exp_{x_i}( t_l * log_{x_i}( m_i ) )
  C[i,c] = d_P(x_i,E_c)^2 + lambda_l * ( d_P(g_i,E_c) - d_P(x_i,E_c) )
  lambda_l = median_{i,c} d_P(x_i,E_c)^2 / median_{i,c} | d_P(g_i,E_c) - d_P(x_i,E_c) |, computed once at the first refresh and then frozen

ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: training sequences (for T), training item latents z_i and Euclidean codebooks e_c^l at refresh time, quotas m_c^l, the frozen 3-vector delta. Outputs: a binary assignment tensor B of shape (N,3) giving one code index per level per item, plus the logged diagnostics (flip count, multiset assertion, collision, prefix entropy).

specification.text:
Offline preprocessing (once, single process, CPU, TRAINING SPLIT ONLY):
  T[i,j] = number of training sessions in which item j occurs in the position immediately after item i (window 1); p_i(j) = T[i,j]/sum_j T[i,j].
  For each level l, take the frozen baseline prefix partition of the training items, build the quotient graph over codes, compute Ollivier curvature kappa_c (W1 between neighbour measures, unit edge lengths) and standardise against 20 member-shuffle nulls that preserve level sizes: z_l = (kappa_obs - mean_null)/sd_null, then centre over levels: delta_l = z_l - mean_l(z_l). The round-3 measured profile [-0.328,-0.071,+0.399] is the expected input.
  t_l = sigmoid(delta_l) in (0,1); written as 3 floats into the Stage-2 config. No tensor is exported, reduced or broadcast inside the training loop at any point.
Assignment refresh r (event-triggered: checked every 10 epochs, fired when the measured hard-assignment flip rate on a fixed 2048-item probe exceeds 0.05, capped at 30 refreshes per level per run; documented defaults):
  1. Euclidean pass over all 24556 training items: z_i, residuals r_i^l, and quotas m_c^l = #{i : c = argmin_c' ||r_i^l - e_c'^l||^2} (the BASELINE rule, so the protected multiset is the Euclidean one; sum_c m_c^l = N exactly, and codes unused by the baseline stay unused).
  2. x_i = tanh(||z_i||) * z_i/||z_i||, E_c = tanh(||e_c||) * e_c/||e_c|| (fixed unit Poincare ball, kappa = 1, no learnable radius, no learnable curvature).
  3. m_i = Frechet mean of the successor points under d_P: 5 Riemannian gradient steps from x_i, step size 1/sum_j p_i(j), projected back to radius 1-1e-3.
  4. g_i = exp_{x_i}( t_l * log_{x_i}( m_i ) ) (geodesic fraction t_l toward the behaviour centroid).
  5. cost(i,c) = d_P(x_i,E_c)^2 + lambda_l * [ d_P(g_i,E_c) - d_P(x_i,E_c) ].
  6. Solve the capacity-constrained allocation by deferred acceptance with capacities m_c^l, obtaining binary B. Assert sum_c B[i,c]=1 for all i and sum_i B[i,c]=m_c^l for all c; abort the refresh (keep the previous B) if either fails.
Training between refreshes: identical to the frozen RQ-VAE except the hard index is B(i,l) instead of the per-step arg-min; STE gradient as in the baseline. Ablation switches: ABL_BEHAVIOUR=0 sets p_i = delta_i (so m_i = x_i, g_i = x_i, bias identically zero); ABL_GEOMETRY=0 replaces d_P by Euclidean norm and m_i by the Euclidean weighted mean (g_i linear interpolation), keeping t_l; both switches default ON.

ideas.title: Geodesic successor pull with capacity-exact (quota-preserving) deferred-acceptance SID assignment

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: SWITCH_BEHAVIOUR = 0 sets m_i^(l) = 0 for all i and l, hence p_i^(l) = origin, H_l(i,k) identical for all k, every rank_H ties at 0 and is broken by code index, C reduces to rank_E, every target equals the item's own triple, no transposition is accepted, and the emitted SID table equals the baseline Euclidean table element-wise. This arm is implemented and unit-tested for exact equality against the baseline SID file; it is never trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: SWITCH_BEHAVIOUR = 1 and SWITCH_GEOMETRY = 1 with the frozen kappa artifact: the full coupled assignment described above. This is the single arm that is trained and evaluated in this round; the two off-switches exist only as code paths and unit tests, no arm is launched with them off.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: SWITCH_GEOMETRY = 0 keeps every behaviour quantity (w_ij, S_i, m_i, the same ball points p_i and q_k, the same candidate sets, the same ranks) and replaces only d_{kappa_l}(x,y) with the Euclidean ||x-y||_2 on the same ball coordinates, which is the kappa -> 0 limit of the Poincare distance up to the factor 2. kappa_l is then unused. This arm is implemented and exercised in a unit test on a fixed toy batch only; it is never trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the TRAINING split only. For each ordered consecutive pair (u_t, u_{t+1}) in every training sequence accumulate t_ij (raw counts, no dedup, no reweighting by position). Popularity margins n_i = sum_j t_ij, m_j = sum_i t_ij. Lift w_ij = t_ij / sqrt((n_i+1)(m_j+1)). S_i = the smallest prefix of the w_ij-sorted successors whose cumulative weight reaches 50% of sum_j w_ij, capped at 16 (B_i = min(16, b_i), floor 1). Then m_i^(l) = sum_{j in S_i} w_ij c^(l)_{e_l(j)} / sum_{j in S_i} w_ij using the FROZEN BASELINE assignment e_l (this breaks the circularity: the centroid never depends on the permutation being optimised). Items with empty S_i get m_i^(l) = 0.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted directed successor lift over training sequences, turned into a per-item successor set S_i with weights w_ij, and thence into a per-level successor-code centroid m_i^(l). Secondary (diagnostic only, never an admission gate): behaviour-conditioned successor agreement at each level.
ideas.cost_estimate: Training cost is 1.00x the baseline at the frozen scale: 24 steps/epoch x 3000 epochs = 72000 steps, and the mechanism adds exactly 0 operations per step (it never touches the encoder, the decoder or the codebook updates; the straight-through path is byte-identical to baseline, which is what makes collapse impossible). The one-off quantisation pass over 24556 items costs: three nearest-neighbour products 24556x(256+7414+20223)x d ~ 2e10 MACs; ~2.4e6 rank/cost evaluations for candidate construction; ~3.1e6 cost evaluations for the swap market (2 passes x 24556 items x 32 holders x 2 evaluations). Total: minutes on one card, few hundred MB chunked, fully vectorisable; measured once and cached.
ideas.coupling_equation: C(i,T) = rank_E(i,T) + sum_{l=1..3} rank_H,l( i, T_l ) with rank_H,l(i,k) = rank of H_l(i,k) = d_{kappa_l}( p_i^(l) , q_k^(l) ) within { H_l(i,k') : T' in Cand_i }, and p_i^(l) = exp_0^{kappa_l}( m_i^(l) / s_l ), q_k^(l) = exp_0^{kappa_l}( c_k^(l) / s_l ), m_i^(l) = sum_{j in S_i} w_ij c^(l)_{e_l(j)} / sum_{j in S_i} w_ij, kappa_l = exp(delta_l). The behaviour term is the w_ij/S_i-driven m_i inside p_i; the curved term is d_{kappa_l} with the measured kappa_l; they multiply/meet only inside H_l, and H_l only enters additively.
ideas.coupling_path: One chain: training transitions -> (w_ij, S_i) -> successor-code centroid m_i^(l) -> exp-map to the behaviour anchor p_i^(l) -> Poincare distance d_{kappa_l}(p_i^(l), q_k^(l)) with kappa_l from the null-standardised measured curvature -> per-level hyperbolic rank -> additively summed with the reconstruction rank into C(i,T) -> the arg-min of C and the transposition gate -> the item's SID triple -> what Stage 3 generates. Removing the behaviour term removes m_i and p_i, all four ranks collapse to the Euclidean rank, no transposition is accepted, and the SIDs are byte-identical to baseline; removing the curved metric (replacing d_kappa by ||p-q||_2 on the same ball coordinates) keeps every behaviour quantity identical and changes the H-orderings, hence the accepted transpositions. Neither component can be deleted without changing the emitted SID table, and the change is a top-1 (indeed top-3) index change, measurable and reportable.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Worth keeping iff (1) the triple multiset is bit-identical to the baseline's while a non-trivial fraction of items (report it; expected order 5-25%) receive a different triple; (2) the mean curved distance from each item to its top successors' triples falls relative to baseline; (3) Stage-3 test_recall@10 rises above 0.055537 and, if the mechanism is right, above 0.065, with the level-1 hit rates and the collision rate numerically unchanged from baseline because they are conserved by construction. If recall moves but the conserved diagnostics also move, the implementation is wrong (a real transposition cannot change them).
ideas.hyperbolic_location: At quantisation, in the code-assignment operator that writes the SID table, after the frozen Stage-2 codebooks exist. The curvature never enters the encoder, the decoder, the codebook update, the straight-through gradient or any radius/scale of the Euclidean code vectors; it acts only inside the ranking function that decides which item receives which already-existing triple.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Per-level trainable-free negative curvature -kappa_l with kappa_l = exp(delta_l) in [0.25, 4] (numerically ~[0.720, 0.931, 1.491] for the measured delta = [-0.328, -0.071, +0.399]), used through (i) the Poincare exponential map at the origin exp_0^kappa(v) = tanh(sqrt(kappa)||v||/2) v / (sqrt(kappa)||v||), and (ii) the Poincare distance d_kappa(x,y) = (1/sqrt(kappa)) arcosh(1 + 2 kappa ||x-y||^2 / ((1 - kappa||x||^2)(1 - kappa||y||^2))).
ideas.key_change: After the frozen Stage-2 RQ-VAE has produced its Euclidean SID table, run one deterministic two-pass descent that transposes whole triples between items whenever the transposition lowers C(i,T) = rank_E(i,T) + sum_l rank_H,l(i,T_l), where rank_H uses the Poincare distance between an item's behaviour anchor and the triple's code points at curvature kappa_l derived from the null-standardised training-split behaviour-graph curvature. Because every accepted move is a transposition, the multiset of triples is invariant, so per-level usage histograms, distinct-triple count and collision rate are exactly the baseline's.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition counts, the successor sets, the quotient graphs and the curvature null distribution are computed exclusively from training-split sequences; no validation or test interaction, item or session is read at any point. The item embeddings and codebooks are the frozen Stage-2 artefacts trained on the training catalogue. The curvature measurement is run ONCE, offline, before the arm starts, on a single process (not inside the training loop), and written to a JSON artifact that every rank reads at start-up, so there is no rank-0-only broadcast or in-loop export; every rank reconstructs identical kappa_l, s_l and q_k from the artifact plus the frozen codebook. Stage-3 is untouched and only measures.
ideas.motivation: The SID table that the generative recommender consumes is produced by a Euclidean arg-min. That arg-min ignores the training behaviour graph, so an item and its regular successors can land in unrelated prefixes, while the quantiser's capacity is allocated by embedding geometry alone. The two measured failures of the previous rounds were (i) curvature spent as a radius, which collapsed the codebook (170 -> 56 distinct triples, recall 0.041888) and (ii) a multiplicative per-pair weight, which moved costs but moved not a single arg-min. The problem this addresses is precisely that: how to make behaviour+curvature change the actual SID indices while the codebook's resolution is untouchable, i.e. frozen as a conserved quantity rather than merely "protected" by a soft plan or a clipped loss.
ideas.novelty: No prior round in this repository changes the *pairing* between items and SID labels while conserving the label multiset. Previous arms moved code vectors (Poincare-Frechet codebook updates), set per-level scaling/radius from curvature (CURVCTRL-SID, BRad-RQ), added successor smoothing or successor boosting to the residual (LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ, succboost-geoshift), used MoE/cone branch structures (BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ, behcone-prefix-rq, TSG-SID) or solved an assignment/transport plan whose arg-max need not reproduce its marginals (CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN, refused). Here the object is a permutation of a fixed bag of whole triples, so the conservation is algebraic, not approximate; the cost is additively rank-fused (no weight to tune); and the measured standardised curvature deviation enters with the deliberately opposite sign to the round-1 arm (kappa_l = exp(+delta_l) instead of exp(-delta_l)), because the level whose behaviour quotient is *flatter* than its size-null is the level that needs the hyperbolic metric supplied, not the level that already has hierarchy.
ideas.observables: (1) top-1/level-wise flip count and flip rate of the emitted triple per item, with behaviour on vs off (must be > 0, reported); (2) equality certificate: the triple multiset, each level's usage histogram, the count of distinct triples and the collision rate must equal the baseline's exactly (integer equality, asserted in code, printed); (3) level-1 hit rates at 0.079/0.005 and collision at 0.177 as an exact-equality check against baseline (they are conserved, so any drift is a bug); (4) mean and median d_{kappa_l}(p_i^(l), q^(l)_{T_l}) over training transitions before/after, expected to fall; (5) successor prefix agreement, i.e. the fraction of training transitions u->v whose level-l tokens now agree or share the modal successor token, recorded per level; (6) total ranked cost C summed over items before/after (monotone decrease by construction); (7) Stage-3 test_recall@10, the only judgement.
risks: The swap market is a local descent and may find few improving transpositions, so the SID table changes too little to matter; the reconstruction rank term may be dominated by a handful of hot triples so most items keep their anchor; the frozen codebook means code k's vector no longer matches its members, raising distortion (the rank_E term only bounds this locally, and a large swap gain could still buy a bad distortion); the behaviour graph is sparse and lift-adjusted top-B successors may be noisy for tail items; kappa_l = exp(+delta_l) may over-flatten level 1 (kappa = 0.72) so the coarse level contributes almost nothing; and the swap step could produce a partition that improves prefix reuse but degrades the reconstruction the encoder was trained for, leaving recall flat or slightly below baseline.
ideas.safeguards: (i) Ball-coordinate clamp: if kappa||x||^2 > 1 - 1e-6 rescale x by sqrt((1-1e-6)/kappa)/||x||; all geometry in float64. (ii) arcosh evaluated as log1p(z + sqrt(z(z+2))) with z >= 0 clamped at 0 to avoid cancellation. (iii) Empty S_i or zero total weight -> m_i = 0 -> p_i = origin -> H ties -> item keeps its Euclidean anchor (no forced move). (iv) No move is forced: a transposition is accepted only if the summed ranked cost strictly decreases, so the descent is monotone and terminating; if no improving transposition exists the baseline table is emitted unchanged and this is reported as zero flips rather than treated as an error. (v) Deterministic tie-breaking everywhere (rank, then triple id, then item id, then a fixed hash for holders) so the table is reproducible and rank-independent. (vi) Explicit integer assertions after the pass: triple multiset equality, per-level usage histogram equality, distinct-triple count equality, collision-rate equality; any failure aborts and falls back to the baseline table rather than emitting a corrupted SID set. (vii) kappa clipped to [0.25, 4] and s_l floored at 1e-6 so a degenerate codebook cannot divide by zero; if all code norms are zero the geometry switch degrades to Euclidean and the run reports it. (viii) The curvature artifact is read, never recomputed, at run time, and its producer runs once offline, so no cross-rank synchronisation exists inside the training loop.
ideas.spec_equations: 1) w_ij = t_ij / sqrt((n_i+1)(m_j+1)); S_i = smallest cumulative-50%-mass prefix, cap 16. 2) delta_l = (kappa_hat_l^obs - mean_r kappa_hat_l^{null,r}) / std_r kappa_hat_l^{null,r}, over R = 20 shuffles that permute the level-l code labels among items while preserving the code-size multiset and rebuild the quotient graph with training transition masses; kappa_l = clip(exp(delta_l), 0.25, 4). 3) s_l = median_k ||c_k^(l)||. 4) exp_0^kappa(v) = tanh(sqrt(kappa)||v||/2) v/(sqrt(kappa)||v||), with exp_0^kappa(0) = 0. 5) d_kappa(x,y) = kappa^{-1/2} arcosh(1 + 2 kappa ||x-y||^2 / ((1-kappa||x||^2)(1-kappa||y||^2))). 6) Residual chain for a triple T: r_1 = z_i - c^(1)_{T_1}; r_2 = r_1 - c^(2)_{T_2}; r_3 = r_2 - c^(3)_{T_3}; E(i,T) = sum_l ||r_l - c^(l)_{T_l}||^2. 7) H_l(i,T_l) = d_{kappa_l}(p_i^(l), q^(l)_{T_l}). 8) Cand_i = {T_i^base} U {T_j^base : j in S_i} U {T_j^base : j in NN_8(i)}, capped 32 by Euclidean item distance to i. 9) C(i,T) = rank_E(i,T) + sum_l rank_H,l(i,T_l), all ranks taken within Cand_i U {T}, ties broken by (rank, triple integer id). 10) Descent pseudocode: for pass in 1..2: order items by gain_i = C(i,cur_i) - min_{T in Cand_i} C(i,T) descending, tie by item id; for each i: T* = argmin; if T* == cur_i continue; for j in the first 32 holders of T* (ordered by hash(j) fixed seed): d = C(i,T*)-C(i,cur_i) + C(j,cur_i)-C(j,T*); keep the j with the smallest d; if d < 0: swap cur_i and cur_j, update the triple->holders index. 11) Emit the final cur_i as item i's SID triple.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: frozen item embeddings Z (24556 x d), frozen codebooks C^(1..3), the baseline Euclidean triple table, the training sequences, the cached curvature artifact {delta_l, kappa_l, s_l}. Outputs: a new triple table (24556 x 3) whose multiset of triples is identical to the baseline's, plus a JSON report with flip counts per level, the multiset equality assertion results, before/after mean d_kappa on successor pairs, and the summed cost C before/after.

specification.text: Let Z = {z_i} (frozen Stage-2 item embeddings), C^(l) = {c_k^(l)} (frozen codebooks, l = 1..3), T_i^base = (e_1(i), e_2(i), e_3(i)) the baseline Euclidean triple, K_l = 247/7414/20223 (code counts used at each level). Build from the TRAINING split the successor sets S_i with popularity-adjusted lift. For each level build the baseline quotient graph, measure its Ollivier-Ricci mean curvature kappa_hat_l, standardise it against R = 20 size-preserving member-shuffle nulls to get delta_l, and set kappa_l = exp(delta_l) clipped to [0.25, 4]. Put every used code on the Poincare ball of curvature -kappa_l by exp-map of c_k^(l)/s_l (s_l = median code norm), and put every item at exp-map of its successor-code centroid m_i^(l)/s_l. Candidate triples for item i: its own baseline triple, the baseline triples of its top-B_i successors, and the baseline triples of its 8 nearest items in embedding space, capped at 32. Rank E and the three H terms within that candidate set (+ the triple currently under evaluation), sum the four integer ranks, take the arg-min as the target, and attempt a transposition with the cheapest of up to 32 holders of that target triple; repeat for 2 passes in descending gain order. Output: a new triple per item.

objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

A THIRD exploration of the behaviour-graph curvature, aimed at the two failures the first two rounds measured rather than at a new idea. THE EVIDENCE: (1) The standardised behaviour-graph curvature profile is real and measurable: on the frozen baseline TIGER_RQ-VAE's prefixes the null-standardised Ollivier curvature of the training behaviour quotient graph is kappa_hat = [-2.32, -1.80, -0.86] over the three levels, i.e. the baseline's fine level is LESS curved than its size-preserving null; the mean-zero deviation gives delta = [-0.328, -0.071, +0.399] and a per-level curvature of [1.389, 1.074, 0.671]. The raw curvature is unrelated to the recall (Spearman +0.03, p=0.65) because the level sizes differ; only the standardised value carries a signal (the level-1 minus level-3 deviation tracks the recall at -0.20, p=0.0095 over 115 mechanism families), and it adds only about one percentage point of R^2 on top of the plain SID-quality measures, which is why the round-1 arm spent it on the space's radius, the codebook collapsed from 170 to 56 distinct triples, and Stage3 test_recall@10 came out at 0.041888, BELOW the 0.0446 of the arm it inherited and 36% below the 0.065 target. (2) The machine verification REFUSED the round-2 proposal (CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN) at the launch, and it was right: the behaviour entered as a MULTIPLICATIVE per-pair weight on the cost, and the check measured that the margins moved (two of four by 1.0 and 3.6) while NOT ONE arg-min moved -- a rescaling of a distance can only reorder the nearest code when two codes are almost equidistant, so the coupling cannot be certified as a behaviour dependency. (3) The capacity freeze the round-2 proposal used to protect the resolution is only partial: the arg-max of a plan with fixed column sums need not reproduce those marginals. THIS ROUND's question: what makes the behaviour term a PROVABLE dependency and the resolution protection EXACT? Requirements every proposal must meet, each of which is a measured failure of the previous rounds: (a) ADDITIVITY: the behaviour term must enter the assignment as an ADDITIVE bias on the cost (or an equivalent term whose top-1 effect is provable), not as a multiplicative rescaling of a distance; the machine verification must be able to measure that the top-1 indices change when the behaviour signal is switched off, with the change reported; (b) EXACT RESOLUTION PROTECTION: the per-level usage multiset must be protected BY CONSTRUCTION -- an assignment rule whose output has the Euclidean usage multiset exactly, not a plan whose arg-max may not reproduce its marginals; the proposal must show the construction, not assert it; (c) THE CURVATURE IS SPENT, NOT SHRUNK: whatever the curvature does, it must not act as a scale on the codebook's radius (that is what collapsed the codebook), and if the curvature is not spent at all, the proposal must say why the behaviour-graph curvature is then in the mechanism; (d) the curvature measurement must come from the TRAINING split only, must be standardised against a size-preserving member-shuffle null, and must be measured OFFLINE or on every rank, so that no rank-0-only broadcast or export happens inside the training loop (that deadlock killed three launches of the round-1 arm); (e) the three switches (behaviour off, geometry off/Euclidean, both on) must be part of the mechanism, and only the both-on arm is trained. The frozen baseline TIGER_RQ-VAE (247/7414/20223, Stage3 test_recall@10 0.055537) is the reference, and the numbers to beat are its support and its recall; the first-level hit rates must stay near 0.079/0.005 and the collision near 0.177, not the 0.998/0.982/0.980 of the collapsed arms.

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. To address these limitations, we introduce HyperVQ, a novel approach that formulates VQ as a hyperbolic Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) problem, leveraging the exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to mitigate collapse and improve cluster separability. Additionally, HyperVQ represents codebook vectors as geometric representatives of hyperbolic decision hyperplanes, encouraging disentangled and robust latent representations. Mercer kernel is used to map data from input space to reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) by kernel adaptive filter (KAF). The VQ task in SLAM is generally performed using unsupervised methods. We provide an alternative approach trough embedding a semisupervised hyperbolic graph convolutional neural network (HGCN) in the VQ step of the SLAM processes. The SLAM platforms we have utilized for this purpose are fast appearance-based mapping (FABMAP) and oriented fast and rotated short (ORB), both of which rely on extracting the features of the captured images in their loop closure detection (LCD) module. For the first time, we have considered the space formed by these SURF features, robust image descriptors, as a graph, enabling us to apply an HGCN in the VQ section which results in an improved LCD performance. papers.abstract: Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. Hyperbolic geometry offers a natural alternative for hierarchical representations, but naive hyperbolic extensions introduce geometric inconsistencies: non-associative hyperbolic addition prevents consistent residual aggregation, while standard straight-through gradient estimation ignores the geometry of the latent space. We propose a geometry-aware hyperbolic residual quantization that addresses these issues in both the forward and backward passes. In the forward pass, Hyperbolic Residual Aggregation restores the telescoping behavior of residual quantization on the Poincare ball. Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications.
